discovery: Development of optical lattice atomic clocks enabling precision timekeeping at the 10^-18 level
rationale: Recent prizes covered superconducting quantum circuits (2025), neural networks (2024), attosecond physics (2023) and entanglement (2022), so the committee can return to precision AMO physics. Optical lattice clocks are a mature, high-impact advance in metrology, relevant to redefining the SI second and to tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock, and Ye pushed it to record precision; both hold major prizes (Breakthrough Prize 2022) and are frequent Nobel shortlist names.
